title: Gasoline sales restrictions now cover 58 of 89 Russian regions as export ban continues
detail: Russia's gasoline and diesel export ban — running through January 31, 2027 — remains in force even as domestic sales restrictions spread to 58 of Russia's 89 regions, with 18 more reporting localized shortages or price increases. The export ban carves out deliveries under intergovernmental agreements: Russia agreed to deliver an additional 25 tonnes of AI-92 gasoline and 5 tonnes of jet fuel to Mongolia by the end of the month. Refining capacity has fallen to its lowest level since 2002, roughly a third below seasonal demand, with domestic gasoline production covering only 65-70% of summer demand as of early July. To offset the shortfall, Russia has ramped up gasoline imports from India (about a third of total imports) and Belarus, with August imports reaching roughly 270,000 tonnes.

title: Putin acknowledges 'certain inconveniences' as restrictions reach 63 of 85 regions
detail: President Putin, asked about the fuel crisis by Vesti journalist Pavel Zarubin, said: "Yes, indeed there are certain inconveniences for people, but the government, of course, must keep this under control" — his most direct public acknowledgment yet, though he again stopped short of calling it critical. The comment came as gasoline sales restrictions were in place in 63 of Russia's 85 regions, with 19 more reporting localized shortages or elevated prices — affecting more than 70% of the country's filling stations. Deputy PM Alexander Novak said the domestic fuel market had entered a "second stage of tension," acknowledging the brief mid-summer stabilization had not held.
